ctx.x: Yeah, that’s a pretty old fashioned thing, like if I learn to read I’m going to lose my spontaneity.

items.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I played with Tommy Dorsey after Buddy Rich left. ... Buddy Rich, who when he wanted to play for a band could really play for a band, you know, aside from being the brilliant soloist that he was.

ctx.x: But I’ll bet you were playing great time.

I’ll tell you it’s pretty good for a nineteen year old. It’s pretty good. Yeah. I mean naturally there are some things that could be improved, but I think you always feel like that. It’s a good hot band if you ever hear the record. It holds up pretty good today. We had very talented people in that band, really good people. So from there on I moved into a lot of the bigger bands. I played with Tommy Dorsey after Buddy Rich left. And I did Benny Goodman’s first European tour, which has never gotten much notice…

Sims and Toots Thielmans we picked up and an English bass player named Charlie Short, and that was Benny Goodman’s first appearance in Europe in 1950. I mean never – even at the height of his popularity. You know Louis had gone over there from like the late 20’s or early 30’s, he was the king over there. And Benny Goodman, as big as he was here, had never played in Europe. I couldn’t figure out why. And he was hugely received over there. So that was a nice all-star group to work with.
